subject: Performance SLO & benchmark methodology — post-call recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@edgefin.com>, Sophie Leong <sophie.leong@edgefin.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO & benchmark methodology — post-call recap

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible benchmark run scheduled:

Key targets you mentioned:
- Latency: p95 ≤ 250ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens); p99 goal < 500ms
- Throughput: sustain 2k inferred tokens/sec across the fleet (peak windows up to 3k)
- Concurrency: 150–200 simultaneous user requests (spiky traffic expected)
- Streaming: yes — partial token streaming is required for long-form responses

Benchmark methodology we propose to send:
- Prompt sets representative of your workload (chat + long-form generation + embeddings).
- Eval harness: dockerized workload runner that replays requests with fixed seeds and profiles token-level latency (we measure from request received -> final token emitted).
- Measurement definitions: warm vs cold (we'll define warm after 5 sustained runs), per-request token-complete latency, and end-to-end concurrency sweep.

Requested from you:
- Confirm the p95/p99 targets above and any tolerance windows.
- Share 100–200 representative prompt examples (we can accept a sanitized sample).
- Availability for a live bench run next week (we'll run in your environment or our private cluster per preference).

I attached the benchmark deck and a first-pass prompt set (prompt-set-v1.csv) to make this concrete.

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm targets + send sample prompts by EOD Fri, Jul 23.
2) We share dockerized eval-harness + run instructions (including reproducibility flags and seed config).
3) Schedule a 90-min live run with your SRE + our solutions engineer (Neha) — we can do Wed Jul 28 or Thu Jul 29.

CC'ing our solutions engineer and SRE once we lock timing. If you want a quick pre-check on infra/profile, let me know your preferred run mode (your infra vs Redwood Dedicated).

Attachments: edgefin-benchmark-deck.pdf, prompt-set-v1.csv

Best,
Marissa
Principal PM, Performance & Benchmarks
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sophie Leong <sophie.leong@edgefin.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & benchmark methodology — post-call recap

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying questions before we hand over prompt samples:

1) Streaming: when you say partial token streaming, do you stream at token granularity (token-by-token) or at chunk boundaries? We need sub-100ms first-byte latency for streamed responses.

2) Measurement definitions: how do you compute p95/p99 for streaming responses (do you measure time to first byte, time to final token, or both)? We care about initial-first-byte for perceived latency.

3) Warm vs cold cache: can the harness reproduce both scenarios? We want to see cold-start behavior for scaled-out replicas (e.g., after autoscale events).

4) Reproducibility: are the seeds deterministic across runs? Will the harness lock quantization / kernel choices so we can compare apples-to-apples across runs?

5) SLA/tail concerns: any changes to latency distribution under sustained high-concurrency (150+)? We need to understand how graceful degradation looks (fallbacks, model variants).

Sophie and I can assemble a sanitized prompt sample and coordinate an SRE to join the live run. Wed Jul 28 10:00am PT could work on our side if that still fits.

—Daniel
Senior Performance Engineer
EdgeFin

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@edgefin.com>, Sophie Leong <sophie.leong@edgefin.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & benchmark methodology — post-call recap

Hi Daniel — great questions, answered inline below. CC'ing Neha (Solutions Eng) and Rishi (SRE) to pick up the technical details and run coordination.

1) Streaming granularity
- We support token-by-token streaming (we can also switch to configurable chunking for bandwidth optimization). For first-byte latency, we measure both time-to-first-token and time-to-final-token. For your requirement, we'll flag time-to-first-token (should be sub-100ms in happy-path / warm-cache scenarios).

2) Measurement definitions
- For streaming endpoints we report:
  * first_byte_latency (time to first token emitted)
  * completion_latency (time to final token emitted)
  * token_emit_rate (tokens/sec during generation)
- p50/p95/p99 are computed on the specific metric requested; default deck contains p95 completion latency but we will add first_byte p95/p99 as a column.

3) Warm vs cold cache
- Harness supports warm/cold sweeps. Cold scenario: fresh model instance (no KV/prefix cache populated) — we emulate autoscale by spinning new workers. Warm scenario: after N warmup requests (default N=5) we mark instance as warm. We'll include both in the run and provide separate histograms.

4) Reproducibility
- The eval-harness is dockerized (attached eval-harness-v1.tar.gz). It pins seeds, quantization profile, and kernel-selection flags via a config file. We also snapshot the runtime config used for each run. That said, some non-determinism can come from GPU scheduling; we capture enough metadata to make runs comparable (traffic replay with fixed timestamps, seed, and deterministic model config where possible).

5) SLA / graceful degradation
- Under sustained high concurrency we surface per-replica queues, tail-latency histograms, and automatic fallback policies (we can configure to fall back to a lower-cost model variant or spill to a different region). Rishi can share our default degradation behaviors and thresholds.

Next steps:
- I've attached the eval harness and a more complete prompt set (prompt-set-v1.csv).
- Can you confirm Wed Jul 28 10:00am PT for the live run with your SRE? If yes, Neha and Rishi will own the Redwood side of the run and we'll provide pre-reqs.

Attachments: eval-harness-v1.tar.gz, prompt-set-v1.csv

Regards,
Marissa
